newsitem.title: USA: Phillips sets copolymer capacity expansion.
newsitem.headline: Phillips sets copolymer capacity expansion.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co said Friday it was moving ahead with plans to expand production of its K-Resin styrene-butadiene copolymer by 100 million pounds per year, a 40 percent increase.

A new plant will be built for an undisclosed cost next to existing K-Resin facilities at Phillip's Houston Chemical Complex, the company said. The existing facilities have annual capacity of 270 million pounds.
The company said it has authoirized funds to develop detailed engineering plans and order special equipment for the expansion.
Pending approval by directors, construction is scheduled to begin in the 1997 fourth quarter, with production beginning in the first quarter of 1999, Phillips said.
It also said 90 million pounds of K-Resin capacity is being constructed under a license granted to Daelim Industrial Co. Daelim's Yochon, Korea, facility will begin production this year.
Developed by Phillips, K-Resin is a clear, tough material used in a variety of products, including medical components, toys, candy wrap, food packaging, cups and clothes hangers.
